overflow-y: auto; font-size: 50%"} | **Conceptual Element** | **Description** | **This Dissertation** | |--------------------------|--------------------|--------------------------| | **Belief dispersion** | Extremity of particular political beliefs | **Belief dispersion**, Related concepts: *disagreement* (i.e., divergence between individuals on a particular issue) or *extremity* (i.e., a situation in which a group is positioned at an extreme end of a continuum of contention) | | **Belief constraint** | Alignment of individual beliefs into comprehensive systems | **Belief Alignment**, The degree to which beliefs on particular issues can be collapsed into fewer ideological dimensions of conflict; with greater alignment, there are correspondingly fewer peaks. | | **Bimodality** | Distribution of beliefs with two distinct peaks | *(Included under Belief Alignment)* | | **Consolidation** | Alignment of beliefs with political identities | *Neither necessary, nor sufficient condition*, considered outside of the concept | ::: ## Belief Alignment ::: {.cell} ::: ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](defense_files/figure-revealjs/Pair1-1.gif) ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: incremental - Constraint on idea elements, @converse2006 - Dimensionality of ideologies, @vannoord2024, @hare2022, @malka2019 - **Bimodality** ::: ::: ::: ## Inter-Item Alignment Implies Dispersion on Latent Scale {.smaller} ::: columns ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](defense_files/figure-revealjs/Dispersion_anim-1.gif) ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} @baldassarri2008 ![](BG2008.png){width="380"} ::: ::: ## Robustness of Opinion Divides ::: {.cell} ::: ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} **High Belief Alignment (0.7)** ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](defense_files/figure-revealjs/Cor_high-1.gif) ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Low Belief Alignment (0.3)** ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](defense_files/figure-revealjs/Cor_low-1.gif) ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Three Levels of Analysis ::: {style="max-height: 500px; overflow-y: auto; font-size: 50%"} | **Level of Analysis** | **Alignment** | **Dispersion** | **(Consolidation)** | |------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------| | *Individuals* | *Ideological Alignment* (USA)
Alignment of beliefs along the primary liberal-conservative continuum in the U.S. | *Disagreement*
Degree of attitudinal mismatch between individuals | The aim is to establish the connection without invoking identity-based considerations | | *Partisan Camps* | *Ideological Alignment* (Europe)
In European contexts, alignment with ideological orientation in two-dimensional space | *Poles of Ideological Contention*
Focus on partisan camps positioned at opposing ideological extremes | *Partisanship*
Only individuals with partisan identities are studied | | *Mass Societies* | *Issue Alignment*
Opinions collapsing into fewer, coherent ideological worldviews in predefined direction | Using the same measurement, these worldviews exhibit increased divergence | *Ideological Identity Alignment*
Alignment of opinions with self-reported ideological identities | ::: # Individuals ## Research Question - *Is ideological disagreement different?* - For animosity - Nature of disagreement - Affective Polarization -\> **'Other Divide'**, @krupnikov2022 - Recognizable structures in abundance of policies, @converse2006 - Being an ideologue as cognitive shortcut, @lau2001, @kahneman2013 ::: aside This part was published in [**Political Behavior**](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11109-025-10049-z) ::: ## Disagreement Among Ideologues ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} **Belief Alignment** ![](Alignment.png){width="380"} ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Opinionatedness** ![](Centrism.png){width="380"} ::: ::: ## Method {.smaller} - Survey experiments with repeated hypothetical profiles - Profiles mirroring responses - 2000 US respondents (YouGov, PRL) ::: panel-tabset ### Study 1 ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} - January 2024 - eight political issues - DV: Feeling Thermometer ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ![](table.png){width="380"} ::: ::: ### Study 2 ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} - May 2024 - four political issues - DV: Expected Disagreement (Never...Always Disagree) - Sophistication: Guessing unobserved beliefs ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ![](vignette.png){width="380"} ::: ::: ::: ## Animosity ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} - Strong Disagreement: **- 9.1 points** (*SE = 0.31, p \< 0.001*) - Weak Disagreement: **- 2.5 points** (*SE = 0.41, p \< 0.001*) (vignette centrist) , **- 2.2 points** (*SE = 0.25, p\<0.001*) (respondent centrist) ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ![Disagreement By Alignment](BeliefAlignment.svg) ::: ::: ## Expected Disagreement ::: {layout="[50,50]" layout-valign="top"} ![Pooled](s2main0.svg) ![By Sophistication](s2main.svg) ::: # Partisan Camps ## Asymmetry Hypothesis {.smaller} #### Cross-pressured individuals and asymmetry in alignment - Cross-pressured individuals lean to the right, @baldassarri2014, @gidronManyWaysBe2022 - Other motivations for conservatism than policy, @jost2009 \vspace{0.5cm} #### Cleavages and party ideologies - Heterogeneous support for radical right, @oesch2018, @kitschelt2005 - Over-emphasizing immigration, @kirkizh2023, @bustikova2014 ::: aside This part was published in [**European Journal of Political Research**](https://doi.org/10.1111/1475-6765.70016) ::: ## Implications of Asymmetry {.smaller} **Partisan disagreement** - Robust to agenda change - More extensive if both aligned ::: {layout="[50,50]" layout-valign="top"} ![Pole A](poleA.svg) ![Pole B](poleB.svg) ::: ## Methods {.smaller} Partisan alignment with party's ideological orientation [^1] [^1]: i.e., do supporters of culturally conservative parties hold culturally conservative beliefs, and do supporters of economically left-wing parties hold left-wing economic views? 15 countries, 131 parties, in 2008 and 2016 ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} #### As the number of aligned attitudes ![Issue Alignment](density.svg) ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} #### As the interconnectedness of beliefs - Belief network estimation & comparisons - Partial correlations, GEI = sum - For party families, across countries ::: ::: ## Results ::: {layout="[50,50]" layout-valign="top"} ![By Party](positions.svg) ![By Party Family *(Cross-European)*](Networks.svg) ::: # Societies ## Sources of Culture Wars {.smaller} *Why do some societies seem to be embroiled in culture wars, while others are not?* ### Religious Cultures Cultures instead of denominations, differences in social norms and beliefs, @norris2011, @lipset1967 Persistent on the party level, @rovny2019, in economic beliefs, @stegmueller2013 ### Development Postmaterialistic priorities, economic scarcity @inglehart1971 Socialization into (post)materialistic conflict @flanagan2003, @schäfer2022, @ogrady2022 ::: aside This part was published in [**European Union Politics**](https://doi.org/10.1177/14651165251320882) ::: ## Methods ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ![Issue Alignment](diagram3.png) ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ![Ideological Identity Alignment](diagram2.png) ::: ::: ## Issue Alignment {.scrollable .smaller} ::: panel-tabset ### Description ![Issue Alignment](IP_Description.svg) ### Multi-Level Regression ::: {style="font-size: 0.80em"} | Predictor | Morality Estimate | Morality Std. Error | |---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------| | **Intercept** | 0.13 | 0.07 | 0.37 | 0.08 | | Religious Culture \[Mixed\] | 0.03 | 0.06 | -0.13 | 0.04 | | Religious Culture \[Catholic\] | 0.12 | 0.05 | -0.25 | 0.04 | | Human Development \[Middle\] | 0.01 | 0.01 | 0.06 | 0.02 | | Human Development \[High\] | 0.04 | 0.03 | \<0.01 | 0.03 | | Net Migration per 1000 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | Inequality (Gini index) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | Globalization (KOF index) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | *Residual Variance* | | | | | | Country (Intercept) | 0.07 | | 0.06 | | | Data | 0.07 | | 0.08 | | ::: ::: # Implications ## Dangers of Ideological Worldviews {.smaller} 1. Beliefs structured by ideological worldviews are particularly problematic in times of polarization, as ideology fosters both disagreement and animosity 2. The sources of such alignment are varied — rooted in culture or shaped by homogeneity and motivation within individual partisan camps ### What now? - Partisan sorting, increasing ideological constraint over time, and the construction of ideological narratives serve to extend conflict rather than displace it - At the individual level: perceived conflict extent, deep partisan involvement, in-group favoritism, animosity, and intolerance, psychological underpinnings of it ## References ::: {#refs} :::
